c74object.name: mc.syncSuite.virtualspeakers~
c74object.digest: Virtual speakers: hear a speaker layout on headphones (binaural) or as a stereo downmix.
c74object.description: Multichannel version: one multichannel inlet (channel i = speaker i) and one multichannel outlet with 2 channels (left, right). Without speakers_num the layout follows the number of incoming channels. Renders what a speaker layout would sound like, for prototyping multichannel pieces without the speakers. In headphones mode (default) it is binaural: each speaker feed is filtered with the head-related impulse responses (HRIRs) of its speaker's direction and summed for the left and right ear (the virtual loudspeaker method). No room, no reverb, no distance model: just the speakers. Speakers do not move, so every speaker has a fixed filter pair: clean and very cheap (about 0.4% of one CPU core for 16 speakers at 48 kHz). In stereo mode the layout is downmixed to two speakers instead. HRIRs: built-in MIT KEMAR dummy head (diffuse-field equalized, horizontal plane, nearest 5 degree measurement), or any SOFA file; resampled to the running sample rate. Normalization: a speaker straight ahead reaches each ear at -3 dB, like a constant-power centre pan. Layout: speaker_coords, azimuths in degrees, the same message syncSuite.nodes uses and outputs (get_speakers). Without it the speakers sit on an even ring straddling the front (2 = L/R, 4 = quad, 8 = octagon). Any change crossfades over 20 ms. HRIR data: B. Gardner and K. Martin, MIT Media Lab Perceptual Computing Technical Report #280, 1994. SOFA reading: libmysofa (BSD-3-Clause). Licenses in docs/licenses.

objarg.name: speakers_num
objarg.description: Size of the default ring layout. Omit it (or 0) to follow the number of incoming channels. Also the speakers_num attribute.

attribute.name: speaker_coords
attribute.description: The layout, as the speaker_coords message: one azimuth per speaker (deg, 0 = front, clockwise). Empty = default ring. Saved with the patch; can be typed as @speaker_coords -30 30 110 -110.

attribute.name: hrtf
attribute.digest: HRTF set: a SOFA file, or default
attribute.description: default (the built-in MIT KEMAR) or a SOFA file name (in Max's search path) or full path. SimpleFreeFieldHRIR convention (the usual HRIR sets), two ears, any sample rate. For each speaker the measurement closest to its direction on the horizontal plane is used; SOFA azimuths (counter-clockwise) are converted, the ears are taken from the receiver positions and Data.Delay is applied. Normalized like the built-in set, so switching does not jump in level. Filters longer than 25 ms are truncated. Loads on Max's main thread and crossfades in over 20 ms. Saved with the patch; can be typed as @hrtf myset.sofa.

attribute.name: speakers_num
attribute.digest: Number of speakers (0 = follow the input)
attribute.description: Size of the default ring layout when no speaker_coords are given. 0 (default): as many speakers as incoming channels.

inlet.digest: Speaker feeds (channel i = speaker i) and messages
inlet.description: One channel per speaker, in speaker_coords order. If the number of channels differs from the number of speakers a warning is posted: extra channels are ignored, speakers without a channel are silent.

outlet.description: Channel 1 = left ear / left speaker, channel 2 = right.

method.name: speaker_coords
method.description: One azimuth per speaker, in degrees: 0 = front, clockwise (90 = right). Speaker i is the i-th value. Same message as syncSuite.nodes (its get_speakers outputs it). Also an attribute, saved with the patch. With no values the default ring is used again.

method.name: mode
method.description: headphones (default): binaural rendering, listen on headphones. stereo: plain downmix for two speakers: speakers across the front are panned at constant power between hard left (-90) and hard right (+90); rear speakers are folded onto the front and fade to -3 dB at 180. Binaural signals do not work over two speakers, which is why stereo mode exists.

method.name: rotate
method.description: Adds this angle to every speaker (clockwise). Handy to check front/back or to hear the layout from another direction. Default 0.

method.name: hrtf
method.description: "hrtf myset.sofa" loads a SOFA file, "hrtf" alone opens a file dialog, "hrtf default" returns to the built-in MIT KEMAR. See the hrtf attribute.
